\chapter{Communication Complexity --- Public Coin Complexity}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.NewmanTheorem.PublicCoinComplexity
\section{Overview}

This module defines the $\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication
complexity of a two-party function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ and establishes its basic
structural properties: an existential characterization in terms of approximating
protocols, equivalence with the finite-message formulation, and monotonicity in the
error parameter $\varepsilon$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Public-coin communication complexity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p002-b002,
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p011-b003
}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.Protocol.ApproxComputes}
The $\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity of
$f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ is defined as
\[
  \mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f)
  \;=\;
  \inf_{\substack{n \in \mathbb{N},\; p \text{ a protocol on } \mathrm{CoinTape}(n) \\ p \text{ $\varepsilon$-approximates } f}}
  p.\mathrm{complexity},
\]
the infimum (in $\mathbb{N}_\infty$) of the worst-case bit complexity over all
public-coin randomized protocols that compute $f$ with error at most $\varepsilon$ on
every input.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bit bound as existence of an approximating protocol]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_le_iff}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_le_iff}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Internal.enat_iInf_le_coe_iff, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.Protocol.ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function of Alice's input and Bob's input, let
$\varepsilon \in \bbr$ be an error parameter, and let $m \in \bbn$. Then the
$\varepsilon$-error public-coin communication complexity satisfies
$\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f) \le m$ if and only if there exist a length $n
\in \bbn$ and a public-coin protocol $p$ over the coin tape $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ such
that $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ and the worst-case bit complexity of $p$ is at most
$m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower-bound characterisation of public-coin complexity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.le_communicationComplexity_iff}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.le_communicationComplexity_iff}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.Protocol.ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function, let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$, and let $m \in
\bbn$. Write $\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f)$ for the $\varepsilon$-error
public-coin randomized communication complexity of $f$, namely the infimum in $\bbn \cup
\{\infty\}$ of the worst-case bit complexity over all public-coin protocols that compute
$f$ with error at most $\varepsilon$ on every input. Then $m \le
\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f)$ if and only if, for every $n \in \bbn$ and
every public-coin protocol $p$ using a coin tape of length $n$, whenever $p$
$\varepsilon$-computes $f$ its communication complexity satisfies $m \le
\mathrm{complexity}(p)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-message characterization of public-coin complexity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_le_iff_finiteMessage}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_le_iff_finiteMessage}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ofProtocol_complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ofProtocol_run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.toProtocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.toProtocol_complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.toProtocol_run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ofProtocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.rrun, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.toProtocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_le_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Fix an output type $\alpha$, a function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, an error tolerance
$\varepsilon \in \bbr$, and a natural number $m$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error
public-coin randomized communication complexity of $f$ satisfies
$\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f) \le m$ if and only if there exist a coin-tape
length $n \in \bbn$ and a public-coin finite-message protocol $p$ over the shared
randomness $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ such that $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ — that is,
for every input pair $(x,y)$ the probability over the coin tape $\omega$ that $p$
outputs a value other than $f(x,y)$ is at most $\varepsilon$ — and the communication
complexity of $p$ is at most $m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of public-coin complexity in the error]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_mono}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_mono}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_le_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function of two arguments, and let $\varepsilon,
\varepsilon' \in \bbr$ be error parameters with $\varepsilon' \le \varepsilon$. Then the
$\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity of $f$ is at most
its $\varepsilon'$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity:
$\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f) \le
\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\varepsilon'}(f)$, this inequality holding in $\bbn_\infty$.
That is, permitting a larger error tolerance can only decrease the worst-case number of
bits that must be exchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coin-tape bound from a finite-message protocol]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_le_of_finiteMessage}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_le_of_finiteMessage}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.ApproxComputes_eq_ApproxSatisfies, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.toCoinTape, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.toCoinTape_approxSatisfies, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.FiniteMessage.Protocol.toCoinTape_complexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity_le_iff_finiteMessage}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$, $Y$, and $\alpha$ be types, let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, and let
$f : X \to Y \to \alpha$. Fix real numbers $\varepsilon' < \varepsilon$, and suppose $p$
is a public-coin finite-message protocol with shared randomness $\Omega$ and private
inputs in $X$ and $Y$ that $\varepsilon'$-computes $f$, meaning that for every input
pair $(x,y)$ the probability over $\omega \in \Omega$ that the protocol's output differs
from $f(x,y)$ is at most $\varepsilon'$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error public-coin
randomized communication complexity of $f$ satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f) \;\le\; \mathrm{complexity}(p),
\]
where $\mathrm{complexity}(p)$ is the worst-case bit cost of $p$ (a $\beta$-valued
message costing $\lceil \log_2 \abs{\beta}\rceil$ bits) and the inequality holds in
$\bbn \cup \{\infty\}$.
\end{theorem}
